transcript.text:
I would love to help you with that! This is about finding equivalent fractions. 

Look at the denominators, which are the bottom numbers. How do you get from 3 to 6 by multiplying?
It is 4/6 because you multiply the top and bottom by 2 since 3 times 2 is 6. Next one: 2/9 + 4/9?

Spot on with the first one, you got it! 

Now, for 2/9 + 4/9, look at the denominators. Are they already the same?
i think it is 6/18 maybe? i just added the bottom numbers too, this is so confusing

It is totally normal to find that confusing at first! Think of the denominator as the name of the piece, like quarters or ninths. When we add fractions, the size of the pieces doesn't change, so we only count how many pieces we have. 

Since the denominators are both 9, what should the denominator of our answer be?

Remember, the denominator tells us the size of the pieces, like ninths. When we add pieces that are the same size, the size of the piece doesn't change! 

If you have 2 ninths and add 4 ninths, what is the size of the pieces in your answer?
6/9 because the denominator stays the same when you just add the top numbers together. Next one: 1/4 + 1/8?

Brilliant! You nailed it. 

Now for 1/4 + 1/8, the denominators are different. We can't just add them straight away. Can you use what you learned earlier to change 1/4 into a fraction with a denominator of 8?
Is it 2/12? I really do not get why we have to change the bottom numbers anyway, this is so confusing.

That is a great question! Imagine you are adding 1 apple and 1 orange—you can't just say 2 apples because they are different things. Fractions need the same bottom number so the pieces are the same size. 

For 1/4, how do you multiply the bottom 4 to get 8?
